newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African exchange plans rand futures by July 1.
newsitem.headline: S.African exchange plans rand futures by July 1.

text.p: The South African Futures Exchange (Safex) said on Tuesday it expected to launch rand/dollar futures contracts by July 1, after the government gave the nod to the derivative in last week's budget.

Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said in his budget speech that the Reserve Bank would supervise the implementation of the futures contracts, which would initially be traded by offshore residents and authorised foreign exchange traders only.
Specifications for the contracts have already been drawn up, although Safex chief executive Stuart Rees said slight modifications would have to be made before the instruments were introduced.
Rees said the underlying instrument on the futures would be the spot rand/dollar exchange rate, while contracts would be valued at $100,000 each.

Expiry dates would follow the same cycle as equity contracts -- March, June, September and December -- and expiry prices would be determined by taking a notional offer to buy and sell from six authorised dealers at the expiry time, followed by the arithmetic average of the middle four rates.
A Reserve Bank official said that Safex's proposals would be subject to its approval as well as the Financial Services Board and other interested parties.
He said the contracts could be intrdocued before July 1, the date set by Manuel for the implementation of his exchange controls reforms.
"Our deadline is July 1," he said. "The Minister said everything he indicated will be in place by July 1 and anything that can be implemented prior to that, will be."
Rees said the contracts would be listed on Safex and would be separate from those planned by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME), which are expected to be launched in June.

"They will be listed on Safex and traded through futures commission merchants in the U.S., in Britain and Europe via members of Safex and we will be quoting the prices on our automated trading system," he said.
"The CME will be separate and will be inverse to our instruments," he added.

Rees said that at this stage, the only modification that needed to be made to its current specifications was a provision that the contract was only available to foreigners and authorised foreign exchange traders.

"We need to add the rider that the contract is available to foreigners and no South African resident client or member of Safex can hold a position in the contract unless they have an exposure to dollars confirmed by an authorised dealer."
